content.title: Sharp Complexity Thresholds for Network Cournot Competition
content.abstract: We determine the approximation complexity of network Cournot equilibrium as a function of demand degree and the number of firms sharing a market. For common, nonincreasing concave polynomial inverse demands, convex quadratic costs of firms' allocation vectors, and rational total capacities, high-precision approximation is polynomial-time solvable for cubic demands, regardless of market size. Quartic demands remain tractable when each market has at most three firms, and quintic demands remain tractable with at most two. These thresholds are exact: approximation at a fixed positive profit-regret
